question: HQ-1
summary: Real-PSP measurement of VFPU vector-register addressing. Confirms the vreg_indices / vreg_idx decode for every scalar encoding and for fourteen selected wide encodings.

provenance.raw_captures: Retained only in the gitignored private area (oracle/hardware-results/). Deliberately NOT committed; this file carries the published results and their provenance, not the raw capture.

covers: vreg_indices (tools/codegen.py) and its C twin vreg_idx (src/rt/vfpu_interp.c), for the encodings listed here
does_not_cover: mreg_index / mreg_idx -- matrix addressing was not probed
vreg_names -- the separate GetVectorRegs naming space used for the VROT overlap quirk was not probed
the packed-size destination choice oz_n at tools/codegen.py:464 -- it calls the measured function, but which size it passes was not probed
the 498 wide encodings outside the fourteen listed here
measurement_boundary.explicit_non_claim: This does NOT establish that all vector addressing is proven on silicon. 14 of 512 wide encodings were observed.

scalar_rule.measured: all 128 encodings agree with this closed form
scalar_rule.note: Width 1 forces transpose to 0, so the row selector is the full two-bit field.

triple_row_selector.evidence: width 3 E=0x20 -> [0,4,8] (row 0) and E=0x40 -> [1,2,3] (row 1). These are the two cases where a bit-5 selector would give a different answer; E=0x00 and E=0x60 are controls and agree under either rule.

transpose_wraparound.evidence: width 4 E=0x60 -> [8,12,0,4]: lanes 2 and 3 wrap to rows 0 and 1. E=0x40 -> [2,3,0,1] is the same rotation. No saturation, error, or aliasing was observed.
